fb:
Built an extension, added a conservatory or taken down a wall since you moved in?

If so, your buyer's solicitor will ask for the paperwork. In Scotland that usually means the building warrant for the work, and the council's certificate confirming it was signed off.

Guarantees matter too: replacement windows, damp proofing, timber treatment and the boiler.

It is far easier to find these before your home goes on the market than in the middle of the missives, when a missing document can hold things up. If something has gone astray, your solicitor can tell you the options.

I go through this with every seller at the start, so nothing catches you out later.

Book a free valuation at duncanure.co.uk/valuation?utm_source=facebook

fb:
The carpets, the curtains, the garden shed: what goes with you when you sell?

In Scotland, it is agreed in writing. Fixtures, the things fitted to the house, normally go with the sale. Carpets, curtains, blinds, light fittings, white goods and the garden shed are whatever you and your buyer agree.

The list ends up in the missives, so there are no surprises on the date of entry.

My advice: decide early. Note what you plan to take, and anything you would be happy to leave. I make sure buyers know from the start, so it never becomes a sticking point late on.

Book a free valuation at duncanure.co.uk/valuation?utm_source=facebook
